title: Temporal-Spatial MLLM: Extending Visual Geometry Priors to 4D Scene Understanding for Action Prediction and Physical Reasoning
description:
Problem: While Spatial-MLLM demonstrates strong static 3D spatial reasoning from 2D observations, understanding dynamic scenes requires reasoning about how spatial structures evolve over time—critical for physical common sense tasks like predicting object trajectories, collision outcomes, and action consequences. Current MLLMs lack explicit 4D (3D + temporal) representations even when video is available.

Proposed Method: We extend the Spatial-MLLM dual-encoder framework with a temporal motion encoder that extracts optical flow and scene-flow features from consecutive frame pairs using a pretrained flow foundation model (e.g., UniMatch). We propose a 4D fusion module that cross-attends between the spatial structure tokens (from the 3D encoder) and motion tokens across time, producing unified spatiotemporal tokens. Additionally, we introduce a physics-aware frame sampling strategy that selects frames capturing maximal spatial change rather than maximal spatial diversity, complementing Spatial-MLLM's inference-time strategy.

Experiments: (1) Physical prediction benchmarks: IntPhys, CRAFT, and Physion for object permanence and collision prediction. (2) Egocentric action anticipation: EPIC-Kitchens and Ego4D next-action prediction using spatial affordance reasoning. (3) Robotic manipulation planning: evaluating spatial trajectory generation accuracy on RLBench. (4) Ablations comparing static spatial tokens vs. 4D spatiotemporal tokens, and different motion encoder choices.

title: TemporalSpatial-MLLM: Grounding 4D Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video via Motion-Aware Geometry Encoding
description:
Problem: While Spatial-MLLM addresses static spatial understanding from 2D observations, reasoning about how spatial relationships change over time (4D reasoning) remains unsolved. Egocentric video applications (robotics, AR/VR, assistive technology) demand understanding not just scene geometry but how objects move, deform, and interact dynamically—requiring temporal spatial intelligence beyond per-frame depth estimation.

Proposed Method: We extend the dual-encoder paradigm with a third temporal-geometry encoder that captures optical flow and scene flow between frames, initialized from a pretrained motion estimation backbone (e.g., UniMatch or FlowFormer). We propose a cross-temporal attention module that explicitly aligns spatial tokens across selected keyframes, building a lightweight 4D feature volume. A motion-aware frame sampling strategy replaces the static space-aware sampling by prioritizing frames with high geometric change (using scene flow magnitude) alongside spatial diversity. The three streams (semantic, static geometry, dynamic geometry) are fused via a hierarchical connector before being passed to the LLM.

Experiments: (1) EgoSchema and Ego4D-SpatialQA for temporal spatial QA; (2) EPIC-Kitchens for object state-change reasoning; (3) constructed synthetic 4D benchmark using dynamic NeRF scenes with ground-truth spatial change annotations; (4) ablations isolating contributions of scene flow encoder vs. motion-aware sampling. Baseline comparisons against Spatial-MLLM, Video-LLaVA, and GPT-4o.

title: TemporalSpatial-MLLM: Grounding 4D Spatial-Temporal Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs via Dynamic Scene Flow Encoding
description: Problem: Spatial-MLLM excels at static 3D spatial understanding from 2D observations, but real-world applications (robotics, autonomous driving, AR/VR) require reasoning about how spatial relationships change over time — i.e., 4D (spatial + temporal) understanding. This flow encoder captures motion vectors encoding velocity, trajectory, and relative displacement of objects in 3D space. A hierarchical cross-attention connector fuses semantic features, static 3D structure features, and dynamic flow features into unified temporal-spatial tokens. Training: We construct a 4D QA dataset by augmenting existing spatial benchmarks with temporal trajectory annotations from datasets like Waymo, KITTI, and EgoBody. Experiments: We evaluate on object trajectory prediction, relative velocity estimation, collision forecasting, and 4D scene description against Spatial-MLLM and video-LLM baselines, demonstrating clear gains in dynamic spatial reasoning.

title: TemporalSpatial-MLLM: Reasoning About 4D Spatial Change Through Time from Monocular Video
description:
Problem: While Spatial-MLLM excels at static 3D spatial understanding from 2D observations, it lacks the ability to reason about how spatial configurations change over time—critical for tasks like predicting object trajectory, understanding scene deformation, or answering questions like 'how far did the chair move?' or 'which object is approaching fastest?'. This 4D (space+time) reasoning capability is absent from existing MLLMs.

Proposed Method: We extend the dual-encoder architecture with a temporal differential spatial module that computes per-frame depth/geometry estimates using a visual geometry backbone, then explicitly encodes spatial deltas between frames as a third input stream. A lightweight cross-frame attention module learns to associate spatial changes with semantic entities. We augment training data with synthetic 4D question-answering pairs generated from dynamic 3D scene simulators (e.g., Habitat, CARLA) and real video datasets with tracked objects (TAO, Waymo), automatically generating QA about displacement, velocity, and collision imminence.

Experiments: (1) New 4D-SpatialBench benchmark measuring temporal spatial reasoning; (2) Existing video QA benchmarks with motion-related queries; (3) Downstream tasks: ego-motion estimation, moving object distance prediction, robotic manipulation planning from monocular video; (4) Ablations isolating the temporal differential module's contribution versus frame-level spatial reasoning alone.

title: TemporalSpatial-MLLM: Learning Dynamic 3D Scene Understanding from Monocular Video via Spatiotemporal Consistency Rewards
description: Problem: Spatial-MLLM excels at static spatial reasoning from 2D observations, but real-world applications (robotics, AR/VR, autonomous driving) require understanding how 3D structure evolves over time—tracking object motion, inferring scene dynamics, and reasoning about future spatial configurations from monocular video alone. Proposed Method: We extend the dual-encoder architecture of Spatial-MLLM with a temporal geometry module that models spatiotemporal correlations between frames. Specifically, we introduce (1) a lightweight optical-flow-conditioned temporal attention layer that bridges the 3D spatial encoder across adjacent frames, enforcing geometric consistency of depth and structure across time, and (2) a novel GRPO reward based on spatiotemporal consistency—penalizing predictions that violate physical plausibility of object trajectories in 3D space. We additionally propose a dynamic scene sampling strategy that selects frames maximizing both spatial informativeness and temporal motion diversity. Experiments: We evaluate on dynamic spatial reasoning benchmarks including ScanQA-Dynamic, EgoSchema-3D, and a newly constructed VideoSpatial-Bench covering object tracking in 3D, relative motion prediction, and future depth estimation. We compare against Spatial-MLLM, VideoChat2, and LLaVA-Video baselines.

title: TemporalSpatial-MLLM: Grounding 4D Spatial-Temporal Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs via Dynamic Scene Flow Encoding
description:

We introduce a motion-aware frame sampling strategy complementing Spatial-MLLM's space-aware sampling, prioritizing frames with high scene-flow divergence. Training uses a curated 4D reasoning dataset combining synthetic dynamic scenes (Kubric, PointOdyssey) and real driving/manipulation videos annotated with temporal spatial QA pairs, fine-tuned with GRPO.

Experiments: Evaluate on (1) dynamic object tracking and trajectory prediction benchmarks, (2) future state prediction in robotic manipulation, (3) collision forecasting in driving scenarios, (4) ablations isolating the dynamic encoder's contribution, comparing against Spatial-MLLM and video LLM baselines.

title: TemporalSpatial-MLLM: Dynamic 4D Scene Understanding via Spatial-Temporal Consistency Training
description:
Problem: Spatial-MLLM excels at static spatial reasoning from 2D observations, but real-world applications (robotics, autonomous driving, AR/VR) require understanding how 3D spatial structure evolves over time — tracking object motion, detecting structural changes, and reasoning about causal spatial events across temporal sequences. Proposed Method: We extend the dual-encoder framework with a third temporal-spatial consistency encoder that processes optical flow and point-trajectory features (from models like RAFT or CoTracker) alongside the semantic and structural encoders. A novel 4D consistency loss during training enforces that predicted spatial relationships remain physically coherent across time: object depths should evolve smoothly, rigid bodies should maintain structure, and occluded regions should re-emerge consistently. We introduce a spatio-temporal GRPO reward that scores model responses based on both spatial accuracy and temporal consistency of predicted 3D scene descriptions.

Experiments: (1) Novel 4D spatial QA benchmark constructed from dynamic scene datasets (Waymo, EgoExo4D); (2) Temporal object tracking in 3D space; (3) Physical event understanding requiring causal spatial-temporal reasoning; (4) Ablations isolating contributions of each encoder and the consistency loss. Baseline comparisons against Spatial-MLLM and Video-LLaVA variants.

title: Temporal-Spatial MLLM: Grounding 4D Scene Understanding in Egocentric Video via Motion-Aware Dual Encoding

We compare against Spatial-MLLM, Video-LLaVA, and 3D-LLM variants, measuring spatial accuracy, temporal consistency, and reasoning chain quality.

title: Temporal-Spatial MLLM: Extending Visual Geometry Priors to 4D Scene Understanding for Action Prediction and Physical Reasoning
description: Problem: While Spatial-MLLM successfully extracts 3D structural priors from static frames, it treats temporal dynamics as secondary to spatial structure. We additionally propose a physics-aware training objective using contrastive pairs of plausible vs. implausible physical continuations, encouraging the model to reason about causal spatial dynamics rather than static geometry. Experiments: (1) Physical commonsense QA benchmarks (PIQA, PhysBench) comparing against Spatial-MLLM and video MLLMs; (2) Future frame spatial configuration prediction on EPIC-Kitchens and Something-Something-v2; (3) Robot action prediction accuracy on RLBench given egocentric video; (4) Ablations isolating contributions of scene flow, optical flow, and physics contrastive training. title: TemporalSpatial-MLLM: Exploiting Motion Dynamics for 4D Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models

title: Temporal-Spatial Grounding: Teaching MLLMs to Reason About Object Permanence and Motion Trajectories in Dynamic Scenes

Experiments: (1) Novel benchmark: 'DynSpatial-Bench' with questions about object trajectories, future positions, and occlusion reasoning; (2) Existing benchmarks: STAR, NExT-QA for causal/temporal reasoning; (3) Ablation over encoder combinations and sampling strategies; (4) Real-world robotics manipulation planning tasks requiring trajectory prediction.

title: TemporalSpatial-MLLM: Grounding 4D Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video via Motion-Aware Structure Encoding

Problem: While Spatial-MLLM excels at static or short-clip spatial understanding from 2D observations, long-horizon egocentric videos (e.g., AR/VR, robotics manipulation logs) require reasoning about how spatial relationships evolve over time—4D understanding combining 3D structure with temporal dynamics. Current models lack explicit encoding of object motion trajectories and scene deformation across extended sequences.

Proposed Method: We extend the dual-encoder architecture with a third Motion Geometry Encoder that processes optical flow fields and per-frame depth maps (from a pretrained monocular depth model) to extract 4D structure tokens capturing spatial change over time. A temporal attention module fuses these motion tokens with static 3D structure tokens and semantic tokens across the sequence. We also propose a Motion-Aware Frame Sampling strategy that prioritizes frames exhibiting significant spatial change (via flow magnitude thresholds) alongside the existing space-aware sampling of Spatial-MLLM. The model is trained with GRPO on 4D QA tasks: object displacement estimation, trajectory prediction, and before/after spatial relationship changes.

Experiments: We evaluate on Ego4D spatial QA benchmarks, EPIC-Kitchens object interaction tasks, and a newly constructed 4D-SpatialBench dataset of annotated manipulation videos. Ablations isolate contributions of motion encoding, temporal attention, and 4D-aware frame sampling versus Spatial-MLLM baselines.

title: Temporal-Spatial MLLM: Extending Visual Geometry Priors to 4D Scene Understanding for Long-Horizon Video Reasoning
description:
Problem: Spatial-MLLM excels at static spatial reasoning from 2D observations, but understanding how spatial structure evolves over time—crucial for robotics, sports analytics, and autonomous driving—requires 4D (3D + temporal) scene comprehension. Current models treat temporal information superficially, missing how objects move, deform, and interact in 3D space across extended sequences.

Proposed Method: We introduce Temporal-Spatial MLLM, extending the dual-encoder paradigm with a dedicated motion-geometry encoder. Specifically: (1) we extract per-frame 3D structure features via the visual geometry backbone as in Spatial-MLLM; (2) we compute optical flow and scene flow between consecutive frames and encode temporal displacement in 3D space using a lightweight flow-conditioned transformer; (3) a cross-attention fusion module aligns semantic, spatial, and motion streams into unified 4D tokens. We also propose a motion-aware frame sampling strategy that selects frames maximizing both spatial diversity AND temporal motion magnitude, replacing static space-aware sampling for dynamic scenes. Training uses curated 4D video datasets (Waymo, EgoExo4D, Kinetics-400 depth annotations) with temporal QA pairs generated via automated pipelines, fine-tuned with GRPO.

Experiments: Benchmarks on Ego4D spatial QA, Waymo motion prediction, ActivityNet temporal reasoning, and a new 4D Spatial Dynamics Benchmark we construct measuring trajectory prediction, collision anticipation, and 3D object permanence across occlusion events.

title: TemporalSpatial-MLLM: Reasoning About 4D Object Dynamics from Monocular Video via Spatial-Temporal Dual Encoding
description: Problem: While Spatial-MLLM excels at static 3D spatial understanding from 2D observations, it lacks the ability to reason about how spatial relationships evolve over time—critical for tasks like predicting object trajectories, estimating velocities, understanding physical interactions, and answering questions like 'will these two objects collide?' Current MLLMs treat temporal reasoning and spatial reasoning as largely separate concerns, missing the synergy between them. Proposed Method: We extend the dual-encoder architecture of Spatial-MLLM with a third 'temporal-spatial dynamics encoder' that processes optical flow and depth-change maps between consecutive frames to capture 4D motion structure. This encoder is initialized from a pretrained scene flow estimation network. We introduce cross-temporal attention layers that allow spatial tokens from different timesteps to interact, enabling the model to build explicit representations of object motion in 3D space. A physics-informed pretraining objective encourages consistency between predicted future spatial states and observed ones. We also construct a curated 4D reasoning dataset by augmenting existing video datasets with automatically extracted scene flow annotations and temporal spatial QA pairs. Experiments: We evaluate on (1) egocentric activity understanding, (2) robot manipulation trajectory prediction, (3) autonomous driving scene anticipation, and (4) a new temporal spatial QA benchmark measuring 4D relational reasoning, demonstrating clear improvements over Spatial-MLLM baselines.

title: TemporalSpatial-MLLM: Grounding 4D Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video via Motion-Aware Dual Encoding
description:
Problem: While Spatial-MLLM excels at static 3D spatial understanding from 2D observations, egocentric video understanding (e.g., for AR/VR, robotics, assistive AI) requires reasoning about how spatial relationships evolve over time—a 4D problem where both scene geometry and camera/object motion must be jointly understood. Current MLLMs fail at tasks like predicting object reachability after motion, tracking spatial affordances, or answering 'where will this object be in 5 seconds?' from first-person video.

Proposed Method: We extend the dual-encoder architecture with a third motion encoder initialized from an optical-flow/scene-flow foundation model (e.g., UniFlow or similar). This encoder captures temporal displacement fields between frames. We design a cross-temporal attention module that fuses the static spatial encoder features with motion features, producing 4D spatiotemporal tokens. We also propose motion-informed frame sampling that prioritizes frames capturing significant spatial displacement rather than only structural information. Training uses GRPO with a novel 4D consistency reward that penalizes temporally inconsistent spatial predictions.

Experiments: (1) Egocentric spatial QA on Ego4D and EPIC-Kitchens—object distance tracking, spatial relationship changes; (2) Navigation waypoint prediction from egocentric video; (3) Robotic manipulation planning requiring future spatial state estimation; (4) Ablations on motion encoder contribution and 4D consistency reward. We compare against Spatial-MLLM and video-LLM baselines.

title: Temporal-Spatial Grounding: Extending Spatial MLLMs to 4D Scene Understanding via Event-Driven Frame Sampling
description:
Problem: Spatial-MLLM demonstrates strong static 3D reasoning from 2D observations, but real-world applications (robotics, autonomous driving, AR) require understanding how spatial structure evolves over time — i.e., 4D (space + time) scene understanding. Current approaches treat spatial and temporal reasoning independently, missing opportunities to leverage motion dynamics for richer geometric inference.

Proposed Method: We extend the Spatial-MLLM dual-encoder framework with a temporal motion module. Specifically, we introduce a lightweight optical-flow-guided temporal encoder that captures per-pixel motion between frames, complementing the static 3D structure encoder. We replace the space-aware frame sampling with an event-driven sampling strategy that identifies frames with significant structural change (object movement, camera motion, scene transitions) using a differentiable saliency score combining optical flow magnitude and depth-change estimates. A cross-attention fusion layer integrates static spatial tokens with dynamic motion tokens, enabling the model to reason about 4D scene properties such as object trajectories, velocity estimation, and dynamic occlusion.

Experiments: (1) Dynamic object tracking and 3D velocity estimation on Waymo and nuScenes; (2) 4D spatial QA on a newly curated benchmark from EgoVideo datasets; (3) Ablation comparing static vs. event-driven sampling strategies; (4) Downstream robotics manipulation planning in simulated environments (RLBench). We expect significant gains on temporally-grounded spatial queries over the Spatial-MLLM baseline.

title: TemporalSpatial-MLLM: Reasoning About Dynamic 3D Scene Changes Through Purely 2D Video Observations
description: Problem: While Spatial-MLLM excels at static spatial reasoning from 2D inputs, understanding how 3D spatial configurations change over time—object rearrangement, human-object interaction, scene deformation—remains unsolved. Current MLLMs cannot answer questions like 'how far did the chair move?' or 'did the stack of boxes become taller?' without explicit depth sensors or point clouds. Proposed Method: We extend the dual-encoder architecture with a temporal differential spatial module that computes frame-pair structural changes using the visual geometry backbone. Specifically, we extract per-frame 3D structure features and compute learned spatial delta embeddings between anchor and query frames, capturing dynamic 3D displacements in image space. A temporal attention layer then aggregates these deltas across the video timeline into change-aware spatial tokens, which are fused with semantic tokens from the 2D encoder. We also propose a motion-aware frame sampling strategy that selects frames maximizing spatial state transitions rather than spatial informativeness alone. Training: We construct a dynamic spatial reasoning dataset by augmenting existing datasets (ScanQA, EgoSchema) with temporal change annotations, plus synthetic videos from Habitat and ThreeDWorld simulators. Experiments: We evaluate on temporal 3D QA benchmarks, object displacement estimation, and action-consequence spatial reasoning, comparing against Spatial-MLLM, VideoChat2, and PLLaVA.

title: Temporal-Spatial MLLM: Extending Visual Geometry Priors to 4D Dynamic Scene Understanding
description:
Problem: Spatial-MLLM excels at static 3D spatial reasoning from 2D observations, but real-world applications (robotics, autonomous driving, AR/VR) require understanding dynamic 4D scenes where object geometry, motion trajectories, and spatial relationships change over time. Current approaches treat temporal and spatial reasoning as largely separate challenges.

Proposed Method: We extend the dual-encoder architecture of Spatial-MLLM with a 4D dynamic encoder that jointly models spatial structure and temporal motion. Specifically, we initialize a motion-aware encoder from a video-based visual geometry foundation model (e.g., a dynamic point cloud estimator or scene flow network) alongside the existing static spatial encoder. A 4D connector fuses semantic features, static 3D structure features, and dynamic motion features into unified spatio-temporal tokens. We introduce a motion-aware frame sampling strategy that selects frames capturing maximal geometric change rather than just spatial diversity. Training incorporates tasks requiring dynamic spatial reasoning: predicting object trajectories in 3D, estimating relative velocities, and answering counterfactual questions about moving scenes.

Experiments: We evaluate on (1) dynamic object localization benchmarks, (2) 3D trajectory prediction from monocular video, (3) temporal depth consistency tasks, (4) robotics manipulation datasets requiring motion prediction, and (5) newly constructed QA benchmarks probing dynamic spatial reasoning. Ablations isolate contributions of the motion encoder, 4D connector, and sampling strategy.

title: TemporalSpatial-MLLM: Grounding 4D Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video via Motion-Aware Dual Encoding
description: Problem: While Spatial-MLLM successfully extracts 3D structure from static or short video clips, egocentric video (e.g., from AR/VR headsets or robots) requires understanding how spatial relationships evolve over time—4D reasoning combining geometry and motion dynamics. Current approaches treat temporal and spatial cues independently, missing how object trajectories, camera ego-motion, and scene deformation jointly define spatial understanding in dynamic environments. Proposed Method: We extend the Spatial-MLLM dual-encoder framework with a third motion-aware temporal encoder initialized from a pretrained optical flow or scene-flow foundation model (e.g., UniFlow). This encoder captures dense inter-frame motion fields, which are fused with the semantic and 3D structural features via a cross-attention connector that explicitly disentangles ego-motion from object-relative motion. We further introduce a 4D-aware frame sampling strategy that selects frames maximizing both geometric diversity (from Spatial-MLLM's strategy) and motion saliency scores. Training uses egocentric datasets (Ego4D, EPIC-Kitchens) augmented with synthetic 4D annotations generated via video depth estimation and SLAM. Experiments: We evaluate on (1) spatial QA in egocentric video, (2) object trajectory prediction, (3) action grounding requiring 3D spatial context, and (4) embodied navigation planning benchmarks, comparing against Spatial-MLLM and VideoLLM baselines.

title: TemporalSpatial-MLLM: Grounding 4D Spatial-Temporal Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs via Dynamic Scene Flow Encoding
description:
Problem: Spatial-MLLM excels at static 3D spatial understanding from 2D observations, but real-world applications (robotics, autonomous driving, AR) require reasoning about how spatial relationships evolve over time — i.e., 4D (3D + time) understanding. Current approaches treat spatial and temporal reasoning largely independently, missing dynamic scene structure like object trajectories, velocity fields, and deforming geometries.

Proposed Method: We extend the dual-encoder architecture of Spatial-MLLM with a third dedicated Scene Flow Encoder that processes optical flow and depth-change signals across consecutive frame pairs, extracting dynamic 3D motion features. These are fused with static semantic and structural features via a temporal-aware cross-attention connector. We introduce a motion-informed frame sampling strategy that selects frames maximizing both spatial coverage and temporal motion diversity, replacing static space-aware sampling. The model is trained with an extended dataset augmented with 4D annotations (ego-motion, object velocity, relative displacement) and optimized using GRPO with rewards targeting dynamic spatial reasoning accuracy.

Experiments: Evaluate on (1) dynamic object tracking and velocity estimation in EgoSchema and NuScenes, (2) 4D spatial QA benchmarks derived from Waymo and ScanNet dynamic sequences, (3) robotic manipulation planning requiring trajectory prediction, and (4) ablations isolating contributions of the flow encoder versus static spatial encoder. Baselines include Spatial-MLLM, Video-LLaVA, and specialized 4D perception models.

title: Temporal-Spatial MLLM: Extending Visual Geometry Priors to Dynamic Scene Understanding via Motion-Aware 4D Encoding
description:
Problem: Spatial-MLLM advances static spatial reasoning from 2D inputs, but real-world applications (robotics, autonomous driving, AR) require understanding how spatial structures evolve over time—capturing object trajectories, scene dynamics, and causal spatial relationships across frames. Current approaches treat temporal and spatial reasoning as largely separate concerns.

Proposed Method: We extend the dual-encoder architecture of Spatial-MLLM with a third motion-aware temporal encoder that computes optical flow and point trajectory features between consecutive frames using a pretrained foundation model (e.g., RAFT or UniMatch). We fuse these motion features with the 3D spatial encoder outputs via a cross-attention temporal-spatial connector, creating unified 4D tokens (3D structure + temporal dynamics). We additionally propose a motion-saliency frame sampling strategy that selects frames based on both spatial coverage (from Spatial-MLLM) and motion discontinuities, ensuring dynamic events are captured under token constraints. Training uses a curated dataset combining Ego4D, Something-Something, and synthetic dynamic scene datasets with spatial-temporal QA annotations, fine-tuned with GRPO.

Experiments: We evaluate on (1) dynamic object localization and trajectory prediction, (2) causal spatial reasoning (e.g., 'which object caused the displacement?'), (3) robotics manipulation benchmarks (RLBench), and (4) egocentric activity understanding requiring spatial context. We compare against Spatial-MLLM and video-specialized MLLMs to demonstrate gains on temporal-spatial tasks.

title: TemporalSpatial-MLLM: Grounding 4D Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs via Motion-Aware Structure Encoding
description:
Problem: Spatial-MLLM excels at static 3D spatial understanding from 2D observations, but real-world scenarios often require reasoning about how spatial relationships evolve over time—e.g., tracking object trajectories, predicting collisions, or understanding scene dynamics in robotics and autonomous driving. Current models lack explicit representations of temporal-spatial change (4D reasoning).

Proposed Method: We extend the dual-encoder framework with a third Motion-Aware Spatial Encoder that captures inter-frame optical flow and scene flow, initialized from a pretrained dynamic scene reconstruction backbone (e.g., MonST3R or DynaMON). A temporal-spatial fusion module cross-attends between static structure features and motion flow features to produce unified 4D tokens. We also introduce a causally-ordered frame sampling strategy that selects frames maximizing both spatial coverage and motion magnitude, replacing the static space-aware sampling of Spatial-MLLM.

Experiments: (1) 4D object trajectory prediction on TAO and KITTI datasets; (2) collision/interaction prediction on Epic-Kitchens and Something-Something-v2; (3) robot manipulation planning evaluation on RLBench; (4) ablations comparing static dual-encoder vs. proposed triple-encoder; (5) few-shot generalization to novel dynamic scenes. We expect 15-20% improvement over Spatial-MLLM on temporal-spatial reasoning benchmarks while maintaining competitive static 3D understanding performance.

title: TemporalFlow-MLLM: Exploiting Optical Flow as a Spatial-Temporal Bridge for Dynamic Scene Reasoning in Multimodal Models
description:
Problem: Spatial-MLLM successfully extracts static 3D structure from video frames, but struggles with dynamic spatial reasoning—understanding how objects move through 3D space over time (e.g., trajectory prediction, collision estimation, velocity inference). Current dual-encoder designs treat spatial features as per-frame snapshots, missing the temporal evolution of geometry critical for robotics, autonomous driving, and sports analysis.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalFlow-MLLM, which augments the Spatial-MLLM dual-encoder architecture with a third optical flow encoder initialized from a pretrained flow estimation backbone (e.g., RAFT or UniMatch). This encoder captures inter-frame motion fields, producing flow tokens that encode directional velocity and acceleration. We design a spatio-temporal fusion module that cross-attends between 3D structure tokens (from the geometry encoder) and flow tokens, producing unified dynamic spatial representations. We also propose a motion-aware frame sampling strategy that selects frames at motion discontinuities rather than spatial diversity, complementing Spatial-MLLM's space-aware sampling.

Planned Experiments: (1) Dynamic spatial QA benchmarks: EgoSchema trajectory questions, nuScenes motion prediction QA. (2) Video-based 3D object tracking accuracy. (3) Collision/interaction anticipation tasks on Something-Something-V2. (4) Ablations comparing static-only vs. flow-augmented encoders, and sampling strategies. We expect substantial gains on motion-dependent spatial tasks while maintaining static spatial performance.

title: TemporalSpatial-MLLM: Grounding 4D Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video via Motion-Aware Dual Encoding
description:
Problem: While Spatial-MLLM excels at static 3D spatial understanding from video, it does not explicitly model how spatial relationships change over time—critical for egocentric activity understanding, robot navigation, and AR/VR applications where objects move and the camera ego-motion creates complex 4D (3D+time) scene dynamics. Existing methods treat temporal and spatial dimensions independently, missing joint spatiotemporal reasoning.

Proposed Method: We extend the dual-encoder architecture of Spatial-MLLM with a third motion-aware encoder that captures optical flow and ego-motion cues extracted via a pretrained monocular depth+flow model (e.g., UniDepth+RAFT). We introduce a 4D scene graph representation that tracks spatial relationships between detected objects across frames, encoded as structured tokens concatenated with spatial and semantic tokens. A temporal attention module learns to correlate evolving 3D structure across sampled keyframes, guided by a motion-saliency frame sampling strategy replacing space-aware sampling.

Experiments: (1) Ego4D spatial QA benchmark measuring object displacement and relative motion reasoning; (2) ScanQA with temporal sequences for object reappearance queries; (3) EPIC-Kitchens hand-object interaction spatial grounding; (4) Ablations on motion encoder contribution, 4D graph vs. flat tokens, and temporal sampling strategies. We expect 10-15% gains over Spatial-MLLM on dynamic spatial reasoning tasks.

title: Temporal-Spatial MLLM: Extending Visual Geometry Priors to Dynamic Scene Understanding via Motion-Aware 4D Encoding
description:
Problem: Spatial-MLLM excels at static spatial reasoning from 2D observations, but real-world applications like autonomous driving, robotic manipulation, and sports analytics require understanding how spatial relationships evolve over time—a 4D (3D + temporal) reasoning challenge that current frameworks insufficiently address. Static geometry priors ignore object motion trajectories, velocity fields, and causal spatial dynamics.

Proposed Method: We extend the dual-encoder architecture of Spatial-MLLM by introducing a third motion encoder initialized from a pretrained optical flow + scene flow foundation model (e.g., UniFlow or FlowFormer). This encoder extracts dense motion fields between consecutive frames, which are fused with spatial structure features via a temporal cross-attention connector that learns motion-conditioned spatial representations. We additionally propose a motion-saliency frame sampling strategy that selects frames capturing peak spatial change events (collisions, occlusions, trajectory inflection points), complementing Spatial-MLLM's structure-based sampling.

Experiments: (1) Dynamic spatial QA on nuScenes and Waymo (predict future positions, relative velocities); (2) Action-conditioned spatial reasoning on Something-Something-v2 (where is object X after manipulation Y?); (3) Sports trajectory prediction from broadcast video; (4) Ablations isolating motion encoder contribution vs. structure encoder. We hypothesize that 4D encoding yields 15-25% improvement over Spatial-MLLM on dynamic benchmarks while retaining static spatial performance.

title: Temporal-Spatial MLLM: Extending Visual Geometry Priors to Dynamic Scene Understanding via Motion-Aware 4D Reasoning
description:
Problem: Spatial-MLLM excels at static 3D spatial reasoning from 2D observations, but real-world applications like robotics and autonomous driving require understanding how spatial relationships evolve over time—4D reasoning combining 3D structure with temporal dynamics. Current approaches treat spatial and temporal dimensions independently, missing critical motion-structure interactions like object permanence, trajectory prediction, and dynamic depth estimation.

Proposed Method: We extend the Spatial-MLLM dual-encoder architecture with a third temporal-motion encoder initialized from optical flow foundation models (e.g., RAFT or UniMatch). We fuse spatial geometry features with dense motion fields via a cross-attention 4D integration module that explicitly models spatial-temporal correspondences. Additionally, we propose a motion-informed frame sampling strategy that selects frames maximizing both spatial geometry information AND motion discontinuities, capturing dynamic scene transitions. Training combines static spatial datasets with dynamic scene benchmarks augmented with pseudo-4D labels generated via monocular video depth estimation and optical flow.

Experiments: (1) Dynamic object tracking accuracy on TAO and BDD100K; (2) Trajectory prediction on nuScenes from monocular video; (3) Dynamic depth estimation on KITTI; (4) Novel 4D QA benchmark testing temporal spatial reasoning (e.g., 'Which object moved closer between frames 2 and 8?'); (5) Ablation isolating contributions of motion encoder vs. static spatial encoder.
